title: Inspect and extend: Address checks before payment planning
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/address.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve bech32 checksum and witness program validation; base58 prefix/length screening; accepted address boundary.
problem: An address is like a destination label with a built-in error check. Follow Bech32 decoding from characters to checksum and witness data, compare the simpler Base58 prefix/length screen, and see how the send screen rejects input before requesting a transaction plan. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/address.ts` and the related project files: src/address.ts; src/screens/SendScreen.tsx.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to bech32 checksum and witness program validation; base58 prefix/length screening; accepted address boundary.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Validation is not ownership proof: the Base58 path checks only prefix and length rather than checksum, and the implementation is not a substitute for audited wallet software.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: An address is like a destination label with a built-in error check. Follow Bech32 decoding from characters to checksum and witness data, compare the simpler Base58 prefix/length screen, and see how the send screen rejects input before requesting a transaction plan.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/address.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
